dimension_literal_resolution.note: single id used for both it1 and it2
single id used for both kt1 and kt2

dimension_literal_resolution.structure: small flat_array of int32 (<=3 ids); membership via linear scan

join_order.notes: Smallest fact table; scan all rows and filter link_type_id ∈ link_type_id_set early
Get t1 row position; reject if pos<0; check t1.kind_id == tv_series_id
Get t2 row position; check t2.kind_id == tv_series_id AND 2005<=production_year<=2008

join_order.probe: movie_info_idx via movie_info_idx__movie_id CSR with key=t1.id
join_order.notes: For mi_idx1: scan range, require info_type_id == rating_id; capture min(info) for surviving (t1,t2) tuples later. Need at least one matching row; track candidate min mi_idx1.info per probe.

join_order.probe: movie_info_idx via movie_info_idx__movie_id CSR with key=t2.id
join_order.notes: For mi_idx2: scan range, require info_type_id == rating_id AND info < '3.0'; track min(info).

join_order.probe: movie_companies via movie_companies__movie_id CSR with key=t1.id
join_order.notes: For mc1: scan range, require cn1_us_bitset[company_id]==1; for each matching mc1 row, lookup cn1.name via company_name__id__pos[company_id] and update min(cn1.name).

join_order.probe: movie_companies via movie_companies__movie_id CSR with key=t2.id
join_order.notes: For mc2: scan range (no filter on company); for each row, lookup cn2.name via company_name__id__pos[company_id] and update min(cn2.name).

data_structures.cn1_us_bitset: bitset(234998) indexed by company_name.id; bit set iff country_code='[us]'
data_structures.link_type_id_set: flat int32 array (<=3 elements), linear search
data_structures.movie_link_primary_csr: mmap uint64[] offsets from indexes/movie_link__movie_id__offsets.bin (used implicitly via raw scan)
data_structures.aggregation: 6 scalar running-min slots: min_cn1_name, min_cn2_name, min_mi_idx1_info, min_mi_idx2_info, min_t1_title, min_t2_title (strings start as empty/uninitialized flag)

indexes.purpose: title id→row position for t1 and t2
company_name id→row position for projection of cn.name
CSR range for mi_idx1 and mi_idx2 per t1/t2 id
CSR range for mc1 and mc2 per t1/t2 id

parallelism.reduction: per-thread 6 running-min strings; final merge takes lexicographic min across threads
parallelism.notes: Driver scan is small (29997 rows) but downstream probes (CSR range reads + varlen reads) dominate; parallelize across movie_link rows.

execution_notes: Order of per-row checks (cheapest first): link_type_id membership → title pk_pos lookups → kind_id check on t1 and t2 (int32 compare) → production_year range on t2 → mi_idx2 CSR probe (smaller selectivity) → mi_idx1 CSR probe → mc1 CSR + bitset → mc2 CSR.

All MIN aggregates require we iterate ALL matching tuples across mc1/mc2/mi_idx1/mi_idx2 combinations (no early exit). However, mins over each axis can be computed independently per (t1,t2) join key, then folded into global mins. Implementation: for each surviving (ml row, t1, t2), compute local mins over mc1.cn.name, mc2.cn.name, mi_idx1.info (filtered), mi_idx2.info (filtered), t1.title, t2.title; then fold into global mins.
Reject (t1,t2) tuple entirely if any of: mi_idx1 has no row with info_type_id==rating_id; mi_idx2 has no qualifying row; mc1 has no row with company_id in cn1_us_bitset; mc2 has no row at all.
cn1 filter is bitset (build once during init) — O(1) probe per mc1 row.
Read varlen projections (t.title, cn.name, mi_idx.info) ONLY after all predicates on that tuple pass.
